items.whyTransfer: The recognition bank for this skill practices Torah verse, Mishnah, Gemara, and commentary (tanakh + rabbinic). A compact legal-code line is a different family: the learner still names the kind of text, but the tells are ruling language rather than verse, mishnah, or analysis.
items.stem:
EXAMPLE — schema illustration, not a production item.

Read this line, then say what kind of text it is:

יִתְגַּבֵּר כָּאֲרִי לַעֲמוֹד בַּבֹּקֶר לַעֲבוֹדַת בּוֹרְאוֹ
"One should strengthen himself like a lion to get up in the morning to serve his Creator." (Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 1:1)

What kind of text is this?
choices: A legal code stating what a person should do.
A Torah verse speaking in Scripture's own voice.
A Mishnah line stating a compact practice rule.
A Gemara line analyzing an earlier stated rule.
items.feedback: It is a legal code: compact language telling a person what to do. That shape is not a Torah verse, a Mishnah question, or Gemara analysis. (EXAMPLE item — not loaded for learners.)

items.label: EXAMPLE — schema illustration, not a production item
items.whyTransfer: Practice for this skill uses Rambam, Yesodei HaTorah 1:1 (thought) and Gemara Berakhot 2a (rabbinic). A psalm line is tanakh: the same 'this source claims that…' move, in a genre the recognition bank never used.
items.stem:
EXAMPLE — schema illustration, not a production item.

Read this line, then finish the sentence "This source claims that…":

יְהֹוָה רֹעִי לֹא אֶחְסָר
"The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." (Psalms 23:1)

Stated as a claim, this is…?
choices: God cares for the speaker as a shepherd does, so the speaker lacks nothing.
The speaker is asking God whether food and safety will arrive by tomorrow.
A later sage is objecting here to an earlier teaching about shepherds.
This line only cites another book and makes no claim of its own here.
items.feedback: Finish 'This source claims that…' first. The psalm asserts that God shepherds the speaker, so the speaker lacks nothing — not a question, an objection, or a bare citation. (EXAMPLE item — not loaded for learners.)
